task.description: You are on branch feature/WF03-ISS0050-20260818 (already created and pushed). Step 0.5 (registry lookup) + Step 1 (diagnose) for docs/issues/ISS-0050.yaml: Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest's 'DropLegacyPublicIdentityTables migration guard (REQ-063 §5)' test (test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs:367) fails intermittently under a FULL-SUITE `mix test` run with `** (Postgrex.Error) ERROR 42P01 (undefined_table) relation "tenant_<hash>.groups" does not exist` raised from inside an Ecto.Migrator.run/4 DDL step, but passes 7/7 when that file is run in isolation (`mix test test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs`). Likely related to ISS-0048 (orphaned tenant_*/sandbox_* schemas accumulating, open, same identity/tenant-provisioning area) but filed as a separate symptom -- confirm or rule out that connection during diagnosis rather than assuming it.

Step 1: reproduce the failure directly -- run the full suite (docker-based, LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED=1 not needed for test DB; use MIX_TEST_PARTITION as needed) enough times to observe the intermittent failure yourself, or find a deterministic repro (e.g. running identity_migration_test.exs concurrently/interleaved with another test file that touches tenant schema provisioning). Trace to root cause: which test(s) running concurrently/adjacently cause the target tenant schema's 'groups' table (or another of the 3 legacy identity tables) to not exist when DropLegacyPublicIdentityTables's guard runs, and why -- e.g. a race between two tests provisioning/tearing down overlapping tenant schema state, async test ordering, a shared fixture not properly isolated, or a genuine bug in the migration guard's own 'has every tenant's row been copied' check.
Write the diagnosis into result.summary: root cause (not just symptom), affected files, and what a fix needs to change. Do NOT implement the fix.
State explicitly whether this shares a root cause with ISS-0048 (orphaned schemas) or is a distinct issue.

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): searched all docs/issues/*.yaml with status: resolved for a matching prior fix. No match found. The only topically-adjacent resolved entry is ISS-0047 (Identity.insert_or_fetch/4 username-index race) -- a different mechanism (application-level on_conflict/unique-index race), not test-isolation/tenant-schema-lifecycle related, so not a match. ISS-0048 (orphaned tenant_*/sandbox_* schemas) and ISS-0050 itself are both still status: open, so no resolved precedent exists for this symptom class yet -- this is the first diagnosis of it.

STEP 1 (diagnose): REPRODUCED DIRECTLY, twice, with live Postgres evidence (not diagnosed from the issue report's prose).

Blocking discovery en route: `mix test` failed to *compile* at all (SystemLimitError, 259-char combined describe+test name in test/letflow/engine_test.exs:717-718, the same class as ISS-0049) -- confirmed pre-existing on origin/main@a553674 itself (git diff origin/main --stat shows this branch differs from main only by an unrelated orchestrator.log line), not introduced by this branch. Fixed directly under core-directives.md's Unblock-Everything directive (this blocked Step 1's own acceptance criteria -- reproducing ISS-0050 needs a compiling suite) and filed as docs/issues/ISS-0051.yaml (status: resolved) per 'No Issue Left Local-Only'; also appended a recurrence note to docs/anti-patterns.md's existing entry for this failure class (now 4 occurrences). This fix is out of ISS-0050's own scope but was necessary to proceed -- flagging it here for visibility, not folding it into ISS-0050's own root cause.

With the suite compiling, ran `mix test` repeatedly (single runs, then an 8-run background loop). Reproduced the exact ISS-0050 failure twice (both in the same run): `** (Postgrex.Error) ERROR 42P01 (undefined_table) relation "tenant_77f0469f83ef4adc8ee14e5a8848e65c.groups" does not exist`, raised from Ecto.Migrator.run/4 inside the DropLegacyPublicIdentityTables guard, on both 'skip-on-uncopied-row' and 'guard PROCEEDS' tests in test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs.

ROOT CAUSE: DropLegacyPublicIdentityTables's guard (priv/repo/migrations/20260819000004_drop_legacy_public_identity_tables.exs, the `DO $$ ... FOR v_tenant IN SELECT tenant_id, schema_name FROM public.tenant_schemas LOOP` block) iterates EVERY row in the GLOBAL public.tenant_schemas registry -- not just the tenant(s) the currently-running test provisioned -- and for each one builds a dynamic `EXECUTE format('... FROM %I.groups ...', ...)` query. Postgres must resolve `%I.groups` (and `%I.users`, `%I.tenant_role`) to a real relation at PARSE time when that dynamic SQL text is executed, regardless of whether any public.groups/users/tenant_role row actually matches that tenant (i.e. even when the WHERE g.tenant_id = %L clause would match zero rows). So ANY row in public.tenant_schemas whose physical schema is missing one of the three tables -- e.g. a tenant that was provisioned via TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 but never (or not yet) had TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/2 run against it -- unconditionally crashes the guard with 42P01 undefined_table the moment the loop reaches that row, with NO relation whatsoever to the tenant the currently-running test actually cares about.

CONFIRMED LIVE: queried the shared letflow_test Postgres database directly (docker exec letflow-postgres-1 psql). Found tenant_id 77f0469f-83ef-4adc-8ee1-4e5a8848e65c registered in public.tenant_schemas with migrations_applied_at = NULL and its physical schema (tenant_77f0469f83ef4adc8ee14e5a8848e65c) genuinely CREATE SCHEMA'd but containing zero tables (confirmed via information_schema.tables -- no groups/users/tenant_role, nothing). This row does not appear anywhere in the logged output of the 8-run background loop (grep -c returns 0 for CREATE SCHEMA/INSERT INTO tenant_schemas mentioning it) -- it predates that loop entirely. Traced its origin: an EARLIER `mix test` invocation in this same diagnosis session was killed by this environment's own 2-minute foreground command timeout (SIGTERM, exit 143) approximately mid-suite -- i.e. after some :auto-mode test's setup had already committed a real, non-transactional CREATE SCHEMA + tenant_schemas INSERT (Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox mode :auto means these writes are real, immediately-committed Postgres state, not rolled back on process exit, per Ecto's own Sandbox moduledoc and this project's own test/letflow/identity/user_test.exs moduledoc, 'Sandbox mode: what ACTUALLY protects against cross-test leakage' section) but BEFORE that test's replay_migrations/2 call and/or its own on_exit DROP SCHEMA/registry-delete cleanup got to run. A SECOND, independent live confirmation of the identical mechanism happened during this same session: killing this diagnosis's own background test-loop process (to stop it after reproducing the bug) left a second incomplete tenant_schemas row (tenant_id 1015c65d-...) behind at that moment -- though that particular one's replay_migrations happened to have already completed its table-creation DDL before the kill landed, so it did not itself trigger the guard bug, it is the same leak mechanism caught mid-flight.

WHY THIS IS 'INTERMITTENT' FROM RELEASE-VALIDATOR'S VANTAGE POINT BUT FULLY DETERMINISTIC GIVEN THE PRECONDITION: the test database (letflow_test / letflow_test<N> per MIX_TEST_PARTITION) is a real, persistent Postgres database shared across ALL `mix test` invocations against it -- not reset between runs. Once any one of the 30+ test files that use Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) (grep -rl "Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)" test/ -- includes test/letflow/tenant_provisioning_test.exs, identity_migration_test.exs itself, engine_test.exs, event_store_test.exs, several definitions/*_test.exs, etc.) is interrupted between its provision_tenant_schema/1 call and its own replay_migrations/2 + on_exit cleanup -- a killed/crashed/timed-out/OOM'd mix test process, a CI job cancellation, ExUnit's own on_exit NOT running because the whole BEAM VM died -- it leaves a PERMANENT orphaned tenant_schemas row with an incomplete physical schema. From that point forward, EVERY subsequent full-suite run against that same database deterministically fails identity_migration_test.exs's DropLegacyPublicIdentityTables guard tests (both the skip-on-uncopied-row and the guard-proceeds test, since both invoke Ecto.Migrator.run/4 against the same guard migration), until the orphaned row is manually purged. This matches RELEASE-VALIDATOR's own observation of the SAME single failure recurring identically across two independent full-suite runs (both hit it, same test, same shape) -- consistent with a persistent DB-level precondition, not per-run randomness. It is silent/undetectable from a single run's own PASS/FAIL signal (a clean `mix test` gives no indication a leaked row now poisons every future run) -- exactly the class of failure docs/anti-patterns.md's 'easy to miss' framing describes elsewhere.

RELATIONSHIP TO ISS-0048 (explicitly confirmed, not assumed): SAME ROOT CAUSE CLASS, DIFFERENT CONCRETE SYMPTOM -- not a coincidental adjacency. ISS-0048 documented ~69-70 orphaned tenant_*/sandbox_* Postgres SCHEMAS (physical schema objects with no owning tenant_schemas registry row -- the registry row is gone, the schema object survives) and explicitly named 'a test that provisions a schema and then crashes/is interrupted before its own cleanup runs' as one of its two suggested candidate causes for that accumulation. ISS-0050's mechanism is the mirror image of that exact same candidate cause: a tenant_schemas REGISTRY ROW survives (provision_tenant_schema/1's own insert genuinely committed) while its physical schema is left incomplete/without the expected tables, because the SAME kind of mid-flight interruption struck between provisioning and full migration replay instead of between provisioning and normal test-end cleanup. Both are instances of one underlying gap: nothing in this test suite's :auto-mode tenant-schema fixtures guarantees cleanup survives an abnormal process termination (kill/crash/OOM/CI-cancel), and the shared, never-reset test Postgres database means any single such leak persists and silently poisons every subsequent run indefinitely. ISS-0050 is more actionable/concrete because it names an exact, reproducible trigger (DropLegacyPublicIdentityTables's guard is the one piece of code in the whole suite that unconditionally scans and dynamically references EVERY registered tenant's schema with zero tolerance for an incomplete one -- ordinary test code only ever touches its own tenant's schema and would never notice a leaked row at all).

WHAT A FIX NEEDS TO CHANGE (not implemented here, for CODE-DESIGNER):
1. (Primary, addresses the deterministic crash directly, also a genuine PRODUCTION robustness gap, not just a test artifact -- a real operator who runs `mix ecto.migrate` for this drop migration while some tenant is mid-onboarding, i.e. genuinely provisioned but not yet migrations-replayed, would hit this identical crash) priv/repo/migrations/20260819000004_drop_legacy_public_identity_tables.exs's guard DO $$ block: before each dynamic EXECUTE format(...) against `%I.groups`/`%I.users`/`%I.tenant_role`, check the target table actually exists (e.g. `to_regclass(format('%I.groups', v_tenant.schema_name)) IS NOT NULL`) and treat a missing table as 'copy not verifiable for this tenant' -- i.e. fold it into the existing v_all_copied := FALSE / skip-the-drop path (matching the guard's own already-conservative 'skip on any doubt' philosophy) rather than letting undefined_table raise uncaught. This is the fix that actually stops the crash, independent of anything else.
2. (Secondary, reduces future leak likelihood but cannot fully eliminate it for a hard-killed process) Audit the :auto-mode test fixtures (test/letflow/tenant_provisioning_test.exs's 'replay_migrations/2 -- successful replay' describe block and its sibling, test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs's provisioned_tenant!/0, and the ~28 other call sites found via `grep -rl 'Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)' test/`) to confirm on_exit cleanup is registered as early as possible after provision_tenant_schema/1 succeeds (before replay_migrations/2 runs) so a normal test failure/exception (not just success) still cleans up -- this narrows the interruption window but a SIGKILL/OOM/CI-cancel of the whole BEAM VM will always bypass on_exit regardless, so this alone does not close the gap.
3. (Immediate/operational, not a code change) The currently-leaked row (tenant_id 77f0469f-83ef-4adc-8ee1-4e5a8848e65c, schema tenant_77f0469f83ef4adc8ee14e5a8848e65c, in the letflow_test database on this host's shared Postgres container) needs to be purged (DROP SCHEMA + DELETE FROM tenant_schemas) as part of landing the fix, or every full-suite run will keep failing even after item 1 ships, until this specific row is removed -- CODE-DESIGNER/ELIXIR-DEV should include this as an explicit deploy/verification step, and TEST-RUNNER should re-verify against a database confirmed free of stale tenant_schemas rows.
4. Consider (worth flagging to CODE-DESIGNER as an option, not mandating it) whether a one-off or CI-startup sweep that purges tenant_schemas rows with migrations_applied_at IS NULL and no matching Registration activity within some age window belongs in this fix's scope or a separate follow-up issue -- ISS-0048's own accumulated-schema-count finding suggests this leak class is not limited to this one guard's blast radius and a systemic sweep may be worth doing once, not scoped to require it as part of THIS fix.
